prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first round I keep the same single-achievement configuration, B021 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case is the discovery chain and not the unanimous openings: the incretin effect and human GLP-1 physiology, proglucagon processing and receptor biology, and identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) amide, followed by drug classes whose benefit on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes has been confirmed in large independent trials. The mechanism is settled and the evidence is mature, so recognition is timely. A physiology-centred citation answers the chair's first question: I can accept it as final, because it says what the three laureates discovered and does not claim to reward drug development. I did not change my preferred configuration. What round 1 changed is how I weigh the alternatives. I now see B033 as limited by Eshhar's absence and by open questions on long-term safety, and I see B032 as having the cleanest attribution but a real objection about what the discovery was.
statement.case_against: The weakest point remains attribution. Priority for the active truncated peptide is contested between Mojsov and the Habener group, and nothing in the record supplied to me settles it. Excluding Knudsen is a policy choice made under the three-person cap, not a scientific finding, and the committee should say so openly. The prize then honours the physiology and peptide identification and not the long-acting analogues that reached patients. If four members judge that translation is the achievement, or that the Mojsov question cannot be defended, this configuration is weaker than it looks. My account of the historical priority is partly recalled and not independently verified.

responses.point: The chair says that if translation must be recognised, the choice is between Knudsen and Mojsov, that he leans towards keeping Mojsov because the active peptide underlies everything downstream, and that he wants round 2 to test whether four members accept a physiology-centred citation.
responses.response: I accept the physiology-centred citation and would vote for it as worded. I also agree on Mojsov for the reason you give: the active peptide is the molecular basis of every later drug, and the record I have shows a contested priority claim, not a refuted one. If the committee wanted Knudsen in, I would only support replacing a name on a stated ground, and I do not think the priority dispute is strong enough to remove Mojsov. A citation about the active form of the peptide, with no wording on who was first, protects the prize against the dispute better than dropping a name would. I also note your statement that you ranked B032 eighth and would back it as a second part. I would not ask GLP-1 to give up a laureate for it, which is why I leave it as an alternative.

responses.point: Linnarsson would keep Knudsen out so that physiology stays separate from industrial development, and he weighs B033 above B032 because it created a new treatment modality.
responses.response: I agree on keeping Knudsen out, for the same reason: if industrial development counts, every other candidate must be held to that standard, and I do not think the record supports drawing that line for GLP-1 alone. On B033 I differ in the weight I give the concerns, not in my assessment of the clinical effect. Eshhar's absence cannot be repaired by choosing June and Sadelain, and long-term safety, secondary malignancy and activity outside haematological cancers are still open. A new modality is a strong reason to expect a future prize, but I read the unresolved credit as the reason it should not take precedence over a trio whose credit is better supported. I do accept that B032's attribution is cleaner than B033's and that B033 is the strongest therapeutic alternative.

responses.point: Perlmann says Knudsen is the most natural fourth name, that Walter and Mori are the better scientific case than SMA antisense, and that she would drop Ishikawa from her cGAS-STING trio, leaving Chen and Barber as the cleanest version.
responses.response: I share your doubts about the cap and I accept your conclusion on it: the development step stays unrecognised, and we should state that. On cGAS-STING I appreciate your move to Chen and Barber, and I still think that pairing is the cleanest form of B015. I have to concede your point that without demonstrated clinical benefit it rests on mechanism alone, and I will not put it in a configuration this year. Your argument for B052 persuades me that the UPR is a general principle with a clean pair. Its translation is indirect, so I treat it as a strong later candidate and not a rival to B021. I also take your doubt on B032: much of its biology came from others. I keep it as an alternative because the Feldmann and Maini pair and the quarter-century of clinical confirmation are unusually clear.

responses.point: El-Manira rejects ranking B032 above CAR-T or optogenetics because it is largely clinical proof of upstream TNF and antibody work, and he now accepts the Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann split for optogenetics as better reflecting discovery versus use.
responses.response: I accept your objection that B032 builds on upstream TNF and antibody engineering, and it is the reason I do not make it my preferred part. I disagree that it should rank below optogenetics on that ground, since B044 has a larger version of the same problem: six credited names, an unresolved split between channelrhodopsin discovery and neuronal use, and little clinical translation yet. I agree that a Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann set better matches the discovery logic than Boyden, Deisseroth and Hegemann. It still leaves Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck unrecognised, which I cannot defend as an arbitrary line. I would not oppose B044 as a second part, but I would not support it as the anchor or at the cost of a GLP-1 laureate.

uncertainties: Whether the supplied record can settle Mojsov versus Habener priority for the active peptide, or whether the citation should just avoid a priority claim.
Whether four members accept excluding Knudsen on stated policy grounds rather than a scientific ground.
Whether a second part (B033, B032 or B044) could win four votes, given that it would force a smaller B021 group.
How the committee should treat B033 without Eshhar, and how much weight long-term safety and secondary malignancy should carry.
statement.conflict_note: I am a rheumatology and autoimmunity researcher, so I have field familiarity with B032 (TNF blockade) and B015 (cGAS-STING and the interferon pathway), and I note a risk of bias toward them. I have not voted for either as a preferred part. My profile shows no documented co-authorship, institutional tie or personal relationship with any candidate on the shortlist, and no recusal-level conflict arose in round 1 for any member. Nothing has changed since round 1.
